note: Per-chapter drafting knowledge, keyed by the chapter IDs in data/drhp_structure.json. NARRATIVE chapters carry an 'instruction' and 'context_fields' used to build a constrained LLM prompt, plus a deterministic 'fallback' so the product works identically with no API key. BOILERPLATE chapters carry 'clauses', standard offer-document text with issuer fields merged in, always marked for merchant-banker finalisation. FACTUAL chapters are built in code from issuer data because they are tables, not prose; they appear here only where they need supporting narrative. Interpolation uses {dotted.path} against the issuer data, plus a {computed.*} namespace of values derived arithmetically from it. A block may carry "when": "computed.flag" or "!computed.flag" to include it conditionally.

I.2.title: Presentation of Financial, Industry and Market Data

clauses.p: Unless stated otherwise, the financial information in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus is derived from the Restated Financial Statements of the Company for the financial years {computed.financialYearsList}, prepared in accordance with the Companies Act and restated in accordance with the ICDR Regulations.

The Company's financial year commences on 1 April and ends on 31 March of the succeeding year. References to a particular financial year are to the twelve-month period ended on 31 March of that year. All figures are presented in Indian Rupees. Figures expressed in crore represent ten million and figures expressed in lakh represent one hundred thousand.

Certain figures have been subjected to rounding adjustments. Accordingly, figures shown as totals in certain tables may not be the exact arithmetic aggregation of the figures that precede them. All percentage figures have been calculated on the basis of unrounded amounts.
All references to "INR", "Rs." or "Rupees" are to Indian Rupees, the lawful currency of the Republic of India. The Company has presented all financial information in Indian Rupees.

Industry and market data used in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus has been obtained from publicly available sources and from industry publications. Such data involves risks, assumptions and limitations, and has not been independently verified by the Company or by the Lead Manager. The data may be defined differently by different sources, and accordingly investors should not place undue reliance on it.

clauses.note: The merchant banker must attribute each industry statistic to a named, dated public source before this chapter is finalised. Statistics carried without attribution are a routine exchange observation.

clauses.p: This Draft Red Herring Prospectus contains certain forward-looking statements. Statements that are not statements of historical fact, and which include words such as "anticipate", "believe", "expect", "estimate", "intend", "objective", "plan", "propose", "project", "seek", "will", "would" or other words or phrases of similar import, are forward-looking statements.

All forward-looking statements are subject to risks, uncertainties and assumptions that could cause actual results to differ materially from those contemplated. Important factors that could cause such a difference include, but are not limited to, the Company's ability to retain its principal customers, movements in the price and availability of raw materials, the Company's ability to fund and commission the capital expenditure described under "Objects of the Issue", changes in the regulatory environment applicable to the {business.industry} sector, general economic and business conditions in India, and the other matters described under "Risk Factors".

Forward-looking statements reflect the Company's current views as at the date of this Draft Red Herring Prospectus and are not a guarantee of future performance. Neither the Company, its Directors, the Lead Manager, nor any of their respective affiliates has any obligation to update or otherwise revise any forward-looking statement to reflect events or circumstances arising after the date of this document.

In accordance with the requirements of SEBI and the SME Platform, the Company and the Lead Manager will ensure that investors are informed of material developments from the date of this Draft Red Herring Prospectus until the date of allotment.

II.1.title: Risk Factors
II.1.instruction: Draft the 'Risk Factors' chapter of an Indian SME IPO offer document. Open with the standard framing paragraph explaining that investors should consider all the information in the document, that the risks described are not exhaustive, and that additional risks not presently known may also impair the business. Then set out the risk factors as a NUMBERED list, each beginning with the number followed by a full stop, and each in its own paragraph separated by a blank line. Write AT LEAST TWENTY separate numbered risk factors where the issuer data supports them. Each risk factor must begin with a bold-free one-sentence statement of the risk in the register of a filed prospectus, followed by two or three sentences of elaboration drawn ONLY from the issuer data supplied. Group the risk factors so that internal risks come before external and industry risks, and issue-related risks come last. Cover, where the data supports it: revenue and customer concentration, with the percentages stated exactly as supplied; dependence on a small number of suppliers; promoter and related-party dependence, including the shareholding percentage and any related-party amount supplied; indebtedness, including the secured and unsecured split; the fact that properties are leased rather than owned where that is stated; intellectual property; litigation; key managerial personnel dependence; capacity utilisation; working capital; regulatory approvals and licences; and the issue-related risks of no prior market, price volatility and dilution. NEVER state that a risk is mitigated, managed, hedged or unlikely unless the issuer data says so in terms. Do not soften a risk with reassurance. Do not invent a figure, a customer name, a proceeding or a covenant that is not present in the issuer data.
must_cover: litigation and regulatory proceedings, if any exist in the data
related-party dependence, if any exists in the data
issue-related risks including SME platform liquidity
issue-related risks including no prior market and dilution

fallback.p: An investment in equity shares involves a high degree of risk. Investors should carefully consider all the information in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus, including the risks described below and the Restated Financial Statements, before making an investment decision. The risks described below are not the only ones the Company faces; additional risks not presently known to the Company, or that it currently considers immaterial, may also impair its business, results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.

The Company has not quantified the financial impact of each risk factor, save where stated. The order in which the risk factors appear is not an indication of their relative importance or of the probability of their occurrence.

fallback.rf: The Company derives a substantial proportion of its revenue from a limited number of customers, and the loss of any of them, or a reduction in the volumes they place, could adversely affect its results of operations. The proportion of revenue attributable to the Company's largest customers is set out under "Our Business".

The Company does not have long-term firm-volume commitments from its customers, and orders are placed against rate contracts or purchase orders. There can be no assurance that historical volumes will continue.

The Company is dependent on a limited supplier base and on the price of its principal raw materials, and an interruption in supply or an increase in input prices that cannot be passed on could affect its margins.

The Company is dependent on its ability to recruit, deploy and retain personnel at the cost assumed in its pricing, and an increase in attrition or in wage costs could affect its results of operations.
The Company's operations are working-capital intensive, and delays in collection from customers or an increase in inventory holding could constrain its liquidity.

The Company's manufacturing operations are concentrated at a limited number of facilities, and any disruption at those facilities, whether from breakdown, fire, industrial action, natural calamity or the loss of a statutory approval, could interrupt production.

The Company's manufacturing facilities have operated below their installed capacity, and there can be no assurance that utilisation will improve or that the capital expenditure proposed will achieve the utilisation assumed.

A portion of the Net Proceeds is to be applied to capital expenditure that has not yet been incurred, and the deployment of those proceeds has not been appraised by any bank or financial institution. Any delay or cost overrun would affect the benefits expected from the Issue.
The objects of the Issue are based on management estimates and on quotations that are not binding, and the actual cost may differ from the amounts stated under "Objects of the Issue".

The Company is party to outstanding proceedings, an adverse outcome in which could affect its business and financial condition. Particulars appear under "Outstanding Litigation and Material Developments".

The Company transacts with entities connected to its promoters, and those relationships may give rise to conflicts of interest. Particulars of related-party transactions appear in the Restated Financial Statements.

The Company has outstanding indebtedness of INR {indebtedness.total_borrowings} crore, and its financing arrangements contain covenants that restrict its operations and may require lender consent for corporate actions.
A portion of the Company's borrowings is secured against its assets, and a default could permit the lenders to enforce that security.
The Company depends on its promoters and a small senior management team, and the loss of their services could affect its operations. {promoters.promoter_details}

The promoters hold {promoters.promoter_shareholding_pct}% of the pre-issue equity share capital of the Company and will continue to exercise significant control after the Issue, including over matters requiring shareholder approval.
The Company occupies certain of its premises on lease rather than as owner, and the non-renewal or termination of any such lease could require it to relocate operations at short notice.
The Company's rights in its intellectual property may be inadequate to protect its business, and it may be subject to claims that it has infringed the intellectual property of others.
The Company requires statutory approvals and licences to operate, and the failure to obtain, renew or comply with the conditions of any of them could interrupt its operations.
Certain approvals required for the Company's operations or for the Issue have been applied for but not yet obtained. Particulars appear under "Government and Other Approvals".
The Company has not independently verified the industry data contained in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus, and that data should not be relied upon as the basis for an investment decision.

The Restated Financial Statements have been prepared for the purposes of the Issue and are not the Company's statutory financial statements, and the restatement adjustments may not be comparable with those of other issuers.
The Company operates in the {business.industry} sector and its performance is linked to conditions in that sector, over which it has no control.

The Company faces competition from organised and unorganised participants, some of which may have greater financial and operational resources, and competitive pressure could affect its pricing and margins.
The Company's operations are subject to extensive regulation, and changes in law, taxation or policy, including changes with retrospective effect, could increase its costs or restrict its operations.
A slowdown in economic growth in India, or an increase in interest rates or inflation, could adversely affect the demand for the Company's products and services and its cost of borrowing.
Natural calamities, pandemics, civil unrest or other force majeure events could disrupt the Company's operations and those of its customers and suppliers.
There has been no public market for the equity shares and an active or sustained trading market may not develop after the Issue.
The Issue price is not indicative of the market price of the equity shares after the Issue, and the price may be volatile. The basis for the Issue price is set out under "Basis for Issue Price".
The equity shares are proposed to be listed on the SME platform, on which trading volumes and liquidity may be lower than on the main board, and the applicable market lot may be larger.
Investors will experience immediate dilution, as the Issue price is higher than the net asset value per equity share before the Issue.
The Company's ability to pay dividends in the future will depend on its earnings, capital requirements and financing arrangements, and there can be no assurance that it will pay dividends.
Any future issue of equity shares by the Company, or any sale of equity shares by the promoters after the expiry of the applicable lock-in, could affect the market price of the equity shares.

IV.2.title: Our Business
IV.2.instruction: Draft the 'Our Business' chapter of an Indian SME IPO offer document. Use sub-headings and cover, in this order: an overview of what the Company does; its products and services; how it earns revenue; its manufacturing or service-delivery operations, including installed capacity and utilisation where supplied; its key performance indicators; its customers and the concentration of revenue among them, stated explicitly with the percentages given; its suppliers and procurement; its intellectual property; its immovable properties, stating clearly whether they are owned or leased; its employees; its competitive strengths; and its business strategies. Write several sentences under each sub-heading rather than one. Where the issuer data gives a list of customers, plants, properties or performance indicators, enumerate the items in full rather than summarising them. Use the formal, restrained register of a filed prospectus, with no marketing language and no superlatives. For revenue from operations, state the value of 'business.revenue_stated' EXACTLY as supplied, without rounding. This is the figure the issuer asserts for this chapter. Do not invent any customer name, number, certification, capacity, property or contract that is not present in the issuer data. Where a sub-heading has no supporting data, state that the particulars are to be supplied rather than filling the gap.
must_cover: immovable properties and whether owned or leased

V.2.instruction: Draft the 'Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations' chapter of an Indian SME IPO offer document. Use sub-headings and cover: an overview; the significant factors affecting the results of operations; a discussion of the results of operations for each financial year supplied, taking revenue from operations, other income, expenses, finance costs, depreciation, profit before tax and profit after tax in turn and comparing each year with the preceding year; the key performance indicators; liquidity and capital resources; indebtedness, stating the secured and unsecured amounts separately where supplied; related-party transactions; capital expenditure and capacity utilisation; and the significant developments after the date of the last balance sheet. For every year-on-year comparison, state both figures exactly as supplied and describe the direction of the movement. Do NOT compute a growth rate, a margin or a percentage change unless that figure is itself present in the issuer data. Use the formal register of a filed prospectus. Do not attribute a movement to a cause unless the issuer data states that cause. Where the data does not support a sub-heading, state that the particulars are to be supplied.

list: An Applicant submits the Application Form to a Designated Intermediary, or applies online through the internet banking facility of an SCSB.

The Application Amount remains blocked in the ASBA Account until the Designated Date, or until the Application is withdrawn, rejected or unsuccessful, and continues to earn interest for the Applicant during that period in accordance with the terms of the account.
The Applicant may not withdraw the authorisation to block, other than in the circumstances permitted under the ICDR Regulations.

clauses.p: A Retail Individual Investor whose Application Amount does not exceed the threshold prescribed by SEBI for the UPI Mechanism may apply through that mechanism. The procedure is as follows:

The Applicant approves the UPI Mandate Request on the UPI application, which blocks the Application Amount in the ASBA Account.
The Applicant must approve the mandate within the time prescribed. An unapproved mandate results in the Application not being considered.

clauses.p: An Applicant using the UPI Mechanism should ensure that the bank account linked to the UPI ID has sufficient balance, that the UPI ID furnished is correct, and that the mandate is approved from the mobile number registered with the bank.

VII.4.title: Restrictions on Foreign Ownership of Indian Securities

clauses.p: Foreign investment in Indian securities is regulated by the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 and the rules and regulations made under it, read with the consolidated Foreign Direct Investment Policy issued by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Government of India, as amended from time to time. Under the current framework, foreign direct investment in most sectors is permitted under the automatic route, subject to the sectoral caps, entry conditions and pricing guidelines prescribed.

Foreign Portfolio Investors registered with SEBI may invest in the Equity Shares subject to the limits prescribed under the applicable regulations, including the limit on the holding of a single Foreign Portfolio Investor together with its investor group, and the aggregate limit applicable to all Foreign Portfolio Investors in an Indian company. Where an investment exceeds the prescribed threshold, it is reclassified as foreign direct investment in the manner prescribed.

Eligible NRIs may invest in the Equity Shares on a repatriation or a non-repatriation basis, subject to the conditions and limits prescribed under FEMA and the rules made under it. An Eligible NRI applying on a repatriation basis must do so through the appropriate account and must furnish the particulars required in the Application Form.

clauses.h: Restrictions on investment from certain jurisdictions

clauses.p: An entity of a country which shares a land border with India, or where the beneficial owner of an investment into India is situated in or is a citizen of such a country, may invest only under the government route, in accordance with the consolidated Foreign Direct Investment Policy. Any transfer of ownership resulting in such beneficial ownership requires government approval.

The issue and transfer of the Equity Shares to a person resident outside India is subject to the pricing guidelines and the reporting requirements prescribed under FEMA. The Company will comply with the applicable reporting requirements in respect of any Allotment made to a person resident outside India.

The Equity Shares have not been and will not be registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933 or under the securities laws of any state of the United States, and may not be offered or sold within the United States except pursuant to an exemption from, or in a transaction not subject to, the registration requirements of that Act and applicable state securities laws.

clauses.note: Foreign investment conditions, sectoral caps and the applicable thresholds change frequently. The Lead Manager and legal counsel must confirm the position applicable to the Company's sector as at the date of the Red Herring Prospectus.

clauses.p: All relevant provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and the guidelines, rules and regulations issued by the Government of India or the regulations or guidelines issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India, established under section 3 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992, as the case may be, have been complied with. No statement made in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus is contrary to the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, the Securities and Exchange Board of India Act, 1992, or the rules, regulations or guidelines issued thereunder, as the case may be.

We further certify that all the statements and disclosures made in this Draft Red Herring Prospectus are true and correct, and do not omit disclosure of any material fact which may make the statements made therein, in light of the circumstances under which they were made, misleading.
Signed by all the Directors of the Company and by the Chief Financial Officer and the Company Secretary and Compliance Officer.

clauses.p: Undersubscription, if any, in any category will be met with spill-over from any other category or a combination of categories, at the discretion of the Company in consultation with the Lead Manager and the SME Platform, subject to applicable law. The Equity Shares reserved for the Designated Market Maker are not available for such spill-over.

clauses.note: The category-wise allocation percentages depend on whether the Issue is made through the book building process or at a fixed price, and on the provisions of Regulation 253 of the ICDR Regulations in force at the time of filing. They are deliberately not asserted here and must be confirmed by the Lead Manager against the final structure of the Issue.

clauses.h: Basis of allocation within a category

clauses.p: Allocation within each category will be made on a proportionate basis, subject to the minimum Allotment being equal to the minimum Application size. Where the number of Applicants in a category exceeds the number that can be Allotted the minimum Application size, Allotment will be made by drawing of lots in the presence of a public representative of the SME Platform, in accordance with the ICDR Regulations.

The entire Application Amount is payable at the time of Application and will be blocked in the ASBA Account of the Applicant until the Designated Date. On the Designated Date, the amount corresponding to the Equity Shares Allotted will be transferred to the Public Issue Account, and the balance, together with the amounts of unsuccessful Applicants, will be unblocked in accordance with the ICDR Regulations and the applicable SEBI circulars.

list: An Applicant may revise an Application during the Bid/Issue Period using the Revision Form, subject to the conditions prescribed under the ICDR Regulations.
Retail Individual Investors may withdraw or lower the size of an Application until the Bid/Issue Closing Date.
Applicants other than Retail Individual Investors may not withdraw or lower the size of an Application at any stage after submission, and are required to pay the Application Amount on submission.
Any revision must be made in the same Application Form and through the same Designated Intermediary through which the original Application was submitted.

clauses.p: If the Company does not receive the minimum subscription prescribed under the ICDR Regulations, including the minimum number of Allottees required for an issue on the SME Platform, the entire Application Amount will be unblocked or refunded in the manner and within the timelines prescribed. If there is a delay beyond the prescribed period, the Company and its directors who are officers in default will pay interest at the rate prescribed under the Companies Act.

clauses.note: This chapter is standard offer-document text assembled around the issue particulars supplied. The Lead Manager must confirm the final category-wise allocation, the minimum Application size, and the market maker reservation against the structure of the Issue as priced.
